data.name: Milap
data.gender_notes: Milap is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Milap is derived from the Sanskrit word 'milapana', which means 'to meet', 'to unite', or 'to connect'. In Hindu mythology, it refers to the union of Radha and Krishna, representing the deep emotional bond between two lovers. The name Milap carries the meaning “Meeting, Union, Connection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Milap usually hope their child will grow to embody meeting, union, connection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine union of the soul with the divine.
data.etymology: Milap belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Meeting, Union, Connection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Milap total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Milap holds significant cultural relevance in India as it is associated with the profound love story of Radha and Krishna. Their union symbolizes the eternal bond that exists between two soulmates and is often depicted in Indian art, literature, and music. This name is also used in various folklore and legends, representing ideals of devotion, passion, and unity. It is a name that evokes feelings of deep emotion and romance and is often given to children to inspire such values.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Milap holds deep spiritual significance as it represents the ultimate union of the soul with the divine. The tale of Radha and Krishna showcases the idea of transcendental love and the union of the individual soul with the universal cosmic consciousness (Brahman). The name Milap is a reminder of the eternal connection between the divine and the soul, representing the journey of the self towards enlightenment and spiritual growth. It symbolizes the unity and oneness of all aspects of life and serves as a reminder of the interconnections that exist between all beings in the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Milap signifies the union or merging of two souls, symbolizing deep love, devotion, and longing for the Divine Beloved. It also represents the sacred bond between two individuals, emphasizing unity, harmony, and companionship.

historical_references.context: Milap is a king in the Mahabharata, who is a friend and ally of the Pandavas. He is also known for his hospitality and generosity.
